reviews.text: All of this is taken from a pre-release version so it may not be representative of the final product [b]The good stuff :[/b] Visuals : The game looks great, environments are especially gorgeous but that was to be expected as Streumon are really good at doing nice looking huge spaces with an occult touch. The character & weapon skins are really cool and I dig the overall art direction. Even when you look closely the world is filled with details and the same goes for enemy models. It can get a bit cluttered when the screen is filled with enemies & your friends' spells, but that's also part of the charm. The main base is especially gorgeous with weird stuff happening beneath your feet and wallpaper worthy vistas. Optimization : Very surprisingly here since it's an Unreal Engine 5 game, but it run very well, with absolutely no stutters. With a 5800x3D / RTX 4070 / 1440p screen I was getting between 60 (at worst) and 100 (most of the time) fps, with very occasional slowdowns in rare circonstances. I'm playing with max graphics, DLSS Quality, no motion blur. You can see for yourself on this raw gameplay I captured : full expedition https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eJzvCsQx2c0 or here, solo but didn't last as long https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nq8QGHjk7f0 Gameplay : The overall game feel is really tight, the game reacts well, hits are weighty, slicing enemies in half or smashing their armor, annihilating enemies with your Wrath (ultimate skills) or killing a spider by parrying its projectile and sending it back to its face feel fricking cool and really gives you the sensation of being a badass E.Y.E. agent. The flow of combat is great and easy to pick up too. The bosses (slight spoiler warning) : [spoiler]The first boss is pretty basic but works well as a run starter. The second one looks very cool and I love the fact that you have to respect its patterns. My only issue is the railgun-like pattern which one shots you, I have no idea how to dodge it and you can't block it (but that may be a me issue). The final boss is also really cool in that respect, and I love that you can deflect his blue blades back at him.[/spoiler] The Blades & Daimons : Each weapon feels unique thanks to the Daimon skills system, getting a new one is always exciting and finding good synergies between you skills is game changing. Run progression : The upgrades system is cool overall with the choice between monoliths / alchemy / daimon heart at the end of every zone, but getting relics can sometimes feel too random (they have cool effects though). Corruption system : The idea is really cool, I just wish it gave run modifiers more often because it shakes up your gameplay and incentivizes you to play well. Meta-progression : Having to find & learn books is pretty cool. At first the drop rate was very low but from the looks of it, that was fixed by sunday already as I got more in one evening than in 11 hours beforehand. Alchemy spells : There may be only 5 right now but they are all useful and the upgrades during the run feel powerful. You really want to pick different ones in coop to cover all uses. The Hermit encounters after each boss : The animations could be a bit sped up (I know you can skip them by clicking but you then risk skipping the scroll effects), but I really dig the idea of him showing up to hinder your run and you trying to fight back. Map variety : There's already a lot of (great looking) different biomes you can step in, we just need more layouts but for an early access release that's great. Objectives : The objectives in each map are already quite varied and it can only get better with time. Sound : The overall sound design is cool, the voices especially sound great, and you can recognize enemies or material drops easily. The music is also good but I didn't hear it enough since it bugs out in coop. The UI : I'm the first surprised here as I thought it was ugly when watching trailers, but it's in fact really good in-game, the only issue is that some fonts look very placeholder but the devs confirmed that they are working to replace them. Netcode : Even if you're not the host, the game works well in coop, there are no enemies teleporting, they react to your hits as well as playing solo, when there is no bug it works very well (I'll get back to it later). The lore : Not much to say here but if you liked E.Y.E. Divine Cybermancy, or dig Warhammer & Lovecraftian / Clive Barker stuff you'll enjoy the game's setting. [b]The not so good stuff :[/b] When you dash, it locks your mouse movement, and even if you get used to it over time it doesn't feel great and it's really annoying. The transition between zoomed in shots & back to idle feels weird, I would really like an option to charge bolts without zooming in. [strike]The forced aimlock on enemies when charging a bolt is really bad on mouse & keyboard, especially on moving enemies as it makes them impossible to get hit, so I end up never upgrading my bolt, which is a shame because it can have a lot of cool effects.[/strike] Fixed already. Counterattack timing : I managed to do like 2 counters in my playtime, parrying is tight but counterattacking just feels like it doesn't work, you never get the special animation, that's a shame. The grapple hook is really cool but can be a bit tricky to aim, it should "stick" a bit more to accessible spots. While I love discovering stuff by playing, some of it is really not well explained or the wording really strange like scrolls with "HP +30% DMG +30% HP +30% DMG +30%" but it only gives +30HP so why the repetition ? Am I getting +30% DMG or just 30 ? The fact that you can't check your stats in-run doesn't help. Also in the ascendency levels, I understand that lvl 2 unlocks the elemental attributes of your weapon, but I have absolutely no idea what does "activate resonant soul 1, 2 & 3" as all the other skills of your Daimon seem to be activated at lvl 1 and there's no reference to "resonant soul" anywhere else in the game. We should be able to open an inventory tab during the run to check our equipped blade & daimon, as well as the relics and buffs we drop during the run. The forge stuff costs way too much in the early game, even with my playtime I'm still not able to craft a single ring or common skin. Also it would be great to have a mean to see our current materials especially before we unlock the forge. Talismans : They are just basic stat sticks, so it's never really exciting getting a new one, it would be great if they added gameplay modifiers kinda like the relics, rings & amulets in Witchfire (stuff like dropping a bomb on dodging, getting a shield that blocks 1 damage every 60 seconds, etc...). The Daimons speaking : The fact they taunt you is great, but you can rarely see it as it's a made up language and the subtitles appear in an unconvenient place. Also there are very few lines and all the daimons seem to have the same personnality but I guess that's EA stuff and it'll get better. Boss variety : I hope alternate bosses will get added because always fighting the same ones in the same order may feel stale over time. Balance : it's all over the place right now with some enemies killing you in one hit out of nowhere (looking at you slicer...), but that's the goal of EA. Falling in lava should be less punishing. You already get the corruption malus of getting revived, so you should get revived somewhere safe. We failed a run that was going very well because one of us slipped in a lava pool and died/revived in chain because he couldn't grapple during the 1 second window he had before dying again. The max FoV could be a bit higher considering the chaos that gets on screen. [i][b]Overall the game is great already, and quite addicting. I love it and just wanna get back to smashing demons & traitors and see what cool loot I can get out of it ! See you Secreta agents in the pit. DEATH TO THE HERMIT ![/b]

[h1]Update 09/10/2025:[/h1] The steam user [url=steamcommunity.com/id/xXCharlzXx]God Emperor Charlax[/url] found a fix for the resolution scaling issues. I can now play in glorious 4K, hooray! A bit sad to see the developers ignored the multiple reports on Steam but it is what it is. Apparently they fixed the issue themselves with the latest update but for some reasons it's still impossible to select our resolution in game, this is unacceptable. Now few words about the game itself since I was able to play it more. Well it's not too bad but it's far from being worth the price at the moment. They already pushed two updates and it massively improved the game, I am still not recommending it because of gamebreaking bugs, more on that later in the review... I enjoy playing it but I cannot in good conscience recommend it yet. The combat and movements are kinda janky to be honest, the grappling hook in particular feels really weird and unresponsive (they fixed the horrible dash with the last patch). Overall the combat is not entirely bad, it can be enjoyable if you can embrace the jank but they absolutely must rework the movements and overall feel of the combat. Sometimes it's really hard to know when we get hit or when our attacks will land. There's obvious issues with hitboxes and weapons reach here. Right now the game is poorly balanced with garbage one shot death by enemies or bosses, it's a complete mess balance wise. Compared to the Fatshark tide games the melee combat is quite underwhelming in Daimon Blades. I don't hate the game and I think it has great potential. The visual style and atmosphere are once again amazing, it's StreumOn Studio so the art style alone is a massive selling point. The graphics are amazing and the game runs very well on my PC. I personally enjoy the non stop action, the gore and pure insanity of the fights with tons of enemies on screen. The procedural generation for the levels is surprisingly good, it's probably the best I've seen for a roguelite in a long while. There's only three bosses right now and they are not particularly interesting to fight. More varied enemies would be nice to see because it all feels very repetitive after few runs. The corruption system is interesting but it's quite a joke to get punished if noobs in your game keeps dying constantly. Currently the game is full of bugs, three times already I got the Door boss which became completely glitched and turned INVINCIBLE! Run ending bugs like that are unacceptable. I was forced to ALT+F4 and I lost three or four books (highly precious loot) and many weapons and materials. A total waste of time and incredibly frustrating to spend a lot of time exploring all the maps entirely just to lose everything because of stupid bugs yeah that left a sour taste in my mouth. When playing co-op there's also tons of issues with random disconnections, crashes and infinite load times and it's very annoying. With that said I would recommend you wait for a discount because in this current state it's not worth the price of admission in my opinion. Once again thanks for the clown awards dumbasses, defending a 35€ game that lacks support for 4k resolution or a resolution selector in 2025 is a new low. Ya'll should be ashamed of yourselves. [code]Original review will stay below for all to see. Human stupidity and fanboys coping in plain sight.[/code] [h1]It pains me to downvote it but I have to.[/h1] For some reasons there is no support for 4k resolution. Someone in the steam forum reported that the developers suggested (on their discord) to use TSR+fullscreen to have 4k. Well after multiple restart and different settings I can say it doesn't work. And to be honest being forced to use TSR while I have a 5090 is quite a joke. I need DLSS or DLAA, plain simple. They are asking for 35€ for this game, we should have resolution options and fully working DLSS. I spent most of my playtime so far trying to edit or tweak the Unreal Engine INI files. Talk about a joke of a release, it was simply not ready. Clown award all you want IDGAF.

Updated review after Patch 11 and a new EGPU (V620 Pro using a 40gbps link) Performance is still pretty middling, its a blurry smearing mess like most other UE5 games and that does not bode well for E.Y.E 2 to be honest. I really hope they move to Cry Engine or Source 2 for that instead. As for the game? I really can only hope they didn't spend too much money on development as this seems to be an abject failure. 530 total reviews 600 peak player count with a current player count of 5 is... Rough. Its hard to blame them but at the same time the lack of advertisement was kinda a terrible move, No Mandalore or Sseth reviews either which can help these weirder smaller games gain attention I think most people at this point know of E.Y.E through them rather than stumbling upon it like I did years ago. The balancing is just awful some of the bosses are an absolute joke while otheres have minions that can 1 shot you from outside your cone of vision from accross the arena after spawning in near silently. Weapon type BARELY matters in reality here is what a weapon needs to be good. No curse, Overblow(extra sword beam), Leeching attacks, Heavy attack armor breaker. If it doesn't have those its not useless but its just worse than other weapons. Beyond that the game is a mess in MP tons of network drops STILL. And a weirdly laggy latency feel even on fast connections with two people living in the same region. Its french jank in the worst ways in the sense of the gameplay isnt innovative or unique but the world and visuals are which is cool but E.Y.E for all of the memes is a fun game. Daimon Blades... Kinda is? I dont think I would buy it again but I will probably try and grind out a god roll weapon and then call it there. TLDR: Holy ♥♥♥♥ Streumon please drop UE5 for EYE2 I beg of you. The only well optimized UE5 game made was arc raiders and thats because they stripped out all of the meme gimmick features out of it. Can't recommend it, performance is awful they straight up have lied about the system requirements tons and tons of bugs, not being able to pick up loot, loot not spawning in the break rooms, hit reg sometimes being utterly useless and a random freezing bug that leaves you unable to move for 5 seconds as the game comes to a halt almost always getting you killed. Its a shame the concept and core gameplay is great but I would wait for some patches.

I want to like this but it's in way too rough a state right now, both technically and with some of its design choices. There are run-ending RNG events between rooms, one-hit-kill traps that aren't synced to the visuals, frequent crashes and disconnects that render the whole run worthless (and this is after the patch to address this), a stationary boss that is way too tanky paired with one-shot mechanics, horrible desync that makes multiplayer feel awful, and numerous bugs that hamper play. I hope they can tune this because there's some really cool ideas here and moments where it all works great, but right now I can't recommend purchasing and playing it in this state.

多人联机没有断线重连，掉出去后什么物资都拿不到，队友复活一样扣腐化值，只比自己复活少几点，但是整体怪物难度提高了好几倍，这完全是不鼓励联机 血瓶补给会导致复活机会减少，再加上砍怪可以回复血瓶，导致没人用，完全是废物设计 愤怒方尖碑就根本没法使用，力量方尖碑的效果之持续一个大层，局内成长没有的情况局外成长只有蚊子腿 盾牌护甲的设计既不能让战斗更有韵律，也破坏爽感 大锤怪莫名其妙的韧性条几乎就是无敌，比BOSS还难打
游戏确实 有很多 问题 闪退 视角锁定 分辨率问题 而且中文内容让人费解 ，但官方一直在积极处理问题 我希望它将是一款好的游戏。

观前提示，本篇评测含大量主观个人看法，并且语气比较冲，因为花了一百多块人民币获得的糟糕游戏体验，我觉得我完全有理由发散一定的怒气来施压制作组改善我以后的游玩过程，如果没有任何变化，我将把其拉入黑名单。 觉得说得有价值可以按个thumb up，认为没有意义可以直接退出不要骂我，如果有不一样看法的话欢迎评论大家一起讨论，毕竟我们都是看好这款游戏想让它越来越好才有机会进行对话。 首先来说一下整体的看法吧，这款游戏底子十分好，但细节层面做得非常差并且走歪路的概率非常大，就现在的游玩体验来看，直接称其为一坨巧克力味道的快餐狗屎也没什么问题，如果制作组不能针对现有的问题快速解决，在一个月内进行一两次版本大更新的话，那这款游戏就等死吧。 1. 肉鸽左上角或者右上角没有小地图：每次我看材料在哪以及自己位置都得按Tab键瞪大眼找，尤其是材料，发光提示完美和环境融为一体，每次找都跟用舌头舔牙缝里的韭菜叶子然后拿手去扣扣不到的感觉是一样的 2. 角色区分不明显，换人物跟换皮肤没区别：你分三个职业每个人物都有自己的故事是好事，但你告诉我仔细一看连个技能树都没有是怎么个事呢，而且你都做出来人物的故事了，结果告诉我连个配音都没有，包括敌人，boss，我在游玩的时候除了在安全屋和NPC聊聊天就没听到过几句人话，毫无代入感 3. build只有武器，还不分每种武器的类别，每换一把武器重新练，肝度指数级上升，甚至每把武器的技能词条都是随机的，怎么，想学无主之地4的几万把枪每把都独一无二是吧，材料一花就是几十个起步结果每次一捡+3，一看就是老贴吧人出身了 4. 多人联机勇气值完全就是累赘，平常单人根本没注意到的东西，联机稍微自己跑远一点，或者跟朋友讲好分头行动突然发现，打怪都完全没伤害只能挨打或者逃跑。拜托，你的打怪回血机制不就是鼓励玩家勇气值暴涨是个怪我就能砍吗，抓紧删掉。只要怪有盾有甲就是大爹，砍到背后都是0伤害。玩家全身都是甲怪砍我一刀都30打底，满打满算升级到20就200血，更别提高难神秘发光斧子哥一刀砍我一百多滴，还是两三个一起刷。音效不明显，前摇提示不明显直接大位移跳到我面前我血条蒸发。 5. 关卡设计更是一坨，竟然还有跳跳乐，是不是不清楚自己定位但是觉得自己是个肉鸽游戏就得让玩家品一品类似别的游戏都有的东西，你可是砍杀游戏，肉鸽的重点不应该放在怪物随机词条上吗，逮着玩家走位整这么难干什么。(随机词条别给我弄得跟隔壁死域一样瞬移远程一个比一个恶心，你这游戏人物性能就摆在那，闪避不仅耗体力还有冷却时间[冷却时间做得刚刚卡手真是谢谢你]) 6. 教程做得也无语，游玩过程中可能出现的因素教程里至少有一半都没展现出来，是想给玩家惊喜吗，适得其反。你哪怕像前作E.Y.E一样给玩家一个图鉴让玩家自己看也行啊，是因为两千年前所以没整出来这项技术吗。 7. 等级加点我就不懂为什么就给32级，人家隔壁鼠疫暗潮是因为有技能树，人物职业有区分，而且还有武器饰品才限制玩家。我请问你有什么？搞个魂系加点最后发现点不点区别根本没有，人家魂5都得90多级以及血源120多级才有资本去高周目里展示技术呢。 8. 多人联机复活队友文字上写的是如果队友拉你起来是不涨腐化条的，但是实际情况就是仍然会加，只不过从2，30点变成+10罢了，我不知道这是不是bug，如果是，请及时修改文本：如果不是，赶紧给我修掉。这是质的区别。 Fin. BOSS部分我说不了，因为就现在的游玩情况来看我根本不敢打后面的boss（你没资格啊，你没资格） 以及游戏服务器问题这些老生常谈的话题我也懒得讲了，制作组在其他评论里应该也能看到类似的问题 这次差评完全是看在热补丁一天一个上对游戏抱有一定的期望才评测的，游戏以后肯定要经历几次大改才能救回来，希望制作组不要放弃
不错，就是音效听起来有点奇怪，其他方面有待提升和改进

TL;DR: Great-looking, okay-feeling, a little tedious, stamped with the classic Streum On kiss of jank. Included art book belongs in the Louvre, game itself boasts about a good binge's worth of play at the moment unless you somehow get seriously stuck in the [strike]cycles of guilt[/strike] gameplay loop. Steam review percentage at time of writing makes for an apt grade, at a C-/D+. There's no sense putting it gently – Streum On's specialty is maximalist kusoge. They cook like it's Iron Chef if the secret ingredient was whatever they tricked a drug boat into throwing overboard by pretending to be the Coast Guard. The rest of the dish? Whatever the drugs made sound really cool this time around. Their art guys do sprawl like nobody else, and they fill every ounce of that sprawl with something interesting to look at. Gaze at any given direction for a minute and soak in enough raw autism to assemble a Lionel train set. The armor, nine times of ten, goes harder than anything previously conceived. Level design comes close to matching the art's ambition, too - tell these nutjobs to render a shed and it'll be big enough to have its own microclimate (though this is downplayed a bit in this one, given its need for ~4min micro-levels). Their writer undoubtedly has a censer loaded with crack rock they swing around the studio like an Orthodox monastic. Localization? Yeah, it's in English, technically - have fun parsing the literally-translated French idioms/diss-track lines. The gameplay is, reliably, whatever the hell the new hotness was around four to five years prior to release, when they were presumably infatuated enough with that given subgenre's ur-example to sit around and vibe-code their own passionate French bootleg of it. By all metrics, these games kind of suck, but they always successfully crowbar the intended idea into your head if you run them, and are remembered a little more fondly than they objectively deserve on that basis. Approached in good faith, they're a good kind of bad, and those with a high capacity for cope can psychically DLSS the whole affair into something genuinely fun. With ~140 hours between E.Y.E and Necromunda and no regrets to speak of, I can attest to the effect myself. Good and/or bad, these guys are a cult-classic factory. With that primer out of the way, I can finally say that Daimon Blades does precisely nothing to shake that pattern. I suppose I can see the vision, though, even if I don't particularly like the execution. More specifically, how quickly what's here exhausts itself. This time around, the intended vibe's a Vermintide-esque dungeon crawler with roguelite progression and trace amounts of what I swear is GunZ: the Duel's Quest mode. Pick a skin, grab a talking weapon (don't worry, they all say the same stuff, it's not Boyfriend Dungeon), enjoy its three attacks, and wade through ten instanced levels full of demons and skeletons to make it back home and upgrade your stats to repeat the process at a higher difficulty. That's the entire gameplay loop, essentially - the core conceit and the problem at large. Hop in, hope for a good spell, dash attack through a field of meat, and repeat step 3 until you get tired. That's Daimon Blades. The objectives are "kill guys," "kill guy," and sometimes a scavenger hunt. Enemy types don't matter, barring the 1-2 demons and 1-2 skeletons with tendencies to two-shot you out the gate - as they're hard to make out in a sea of chaff, the only real advice is to not get caught lacking and leverage dash attacks some more. Once the old man curses you just right or your evil-ass cutlery ramps up your difficulty out of the blue, most of the roster will start hitting hard enough that it all just turns into a big ball of death you watch for any protruding projectile or leap. Story's extant, if as cryptic and fortune cookie-based as ever, but you won't get anything in the middle of a run (as the one game mode's an RNG'd series of instances you pick from sets of 3) and the NPCs are under contract to be aloof and dogmatic. Read whatever you happen to pick up, as it's the only reprieve you'll get from pressing Shift+M1. Bugs aren't ubiquitous, but can certainly blindside you - my latest run was ended by immortal torsos hounding me throughout a level, placing me back into the hub zone, which I promptly fell so deep into that the unstuck button couldn't save me. Shot in the dark - instakills set health to a value too far past whatever the threshold for a kill would be, while the limb-lopping gimmick is some free-floating thing dependent largely on demons just not having a positive HP value. Credit where it's due, that's the only big bug I ran into, so you can bet on a clean enough run by just binning any weapon that's a little too good. Suffice to say, I was forcing myself to keep playing pretty quick (though the game's virtually perfect aesthetic pulled my increasingly indolent ass along like a sled dog). Doesn't take that many runs to realize that you've already effectively played the whole game, excepting that you didn't proc *all* the NPC schizo-babble at the home base. It may, however, take that many runs to be allowed to progress - your mileage may vary, but I've encountered two books some eight hours in, which was a bit of an issue given that those are essential to meta-progression. Anyways, more menacing numbers with more menacing numbers await you and *your* more menacing numbers at the deepest depths, should you choose to try and stretch your dollar on that particular torture rack. Give this one, I don't know, another half a year's updates and check back - it just needs more than it's got unless you've never played a similar game before. Even then, maybe give 'em a sec to prune the worst of the jank.

I recommend this game if you have a good Graphics Card with quite a bit of VRAM, if you don't meet the RECOMMENDED hardware requirements, I'm sorry - there's no "play on low graphics" don't even bother, just look elsewhere, I PROMISE you this. I had a 1060 before I upgraded to an RTX 5060 Ti, and I'd say the game goes from "mud in my eyes, laggy as ♥♥♥♥, can't see ♥♥♥♥" to "a brilliant display of graphics, good gameplay and an addicting gameplay loop". I mean it. I also want you to read this sentence in the game's about text: "Daimon Blades is a brutal first person slasher that combines the depth of action RPGs and replayability of roguelites." If this sounds like your kind of deal, you're in the right place and you'll probably like this game. Now, to the more esoteric part of my recommendation. Have you ever played a Streum Game before? E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy? Deathwing? Necromunda? If so, you'll know what to expect, nothing I can write here will truly explain to you what those games are in terms of how Good they are but also how Broken they are. I can guess how much Methylphenidate is consumed per developer at StreumOn Studio based on the many design decisions of this game. The Lore is given to you in fragments, not to be vague on purpose, but because you probably are canonically brain damaged and that's just what information is to you now. With a remarkable game mechanics like: A Relationship gauge between you and your weapon, each weapon has different personalities and probably hates you to some degree. Hear them bickering with the Door about what's coming up next. It's like having a backseat Chatter in your lower-left chat, a sentinent little potato that thinks it knows better than you - and is happy to tell you so. He'll be smug when you die and he'll tell you how much better he'd do it and how you'd probably kill everyone faster if you placed your knee a little bit more to the right. Have you ever wondered what the enemy was feeling when they killed you? Why, you don't need to wonder anymore, the death screen will tell you the mood of every enemy in the game, including the universe itself - upon killing you. Nothing like a last twist of the knife to know that the Undead Lich Lord was "kind of tired" as he tore your spine out of your chest. Is that really happening? I don't know. What's the lore? Reality exists and demons don't like that, in the future they'll try to break into our world and harass the French on Mars - we need to stop that from happening. We can't, but we can try. To prevent the innevitable, we need to kill the traitors to our Cult, our Cult is the most honest and raw truth of the universe - for it is basically all religions rolled into one and all of them are treated equally, unless they aren't. The Hermit is a real danger to our Future, the reason why might not be apparent at first, but due to extensive autistic obsession with some Hindu trivia, I can explain why one Hermit can be as dangerous as the E.Y.E portray him to be: In Hinduism they have a concept called [The] "Six pramanas"; The Setting of E.Y.E shares a lot of lore with Hinduism and other religions, which means that the games internal logic syncs up very well with the Six pramanas, which means "Correct Knowledge and Truth" there are some things in the world of E.Y.E that are KNOWN and there are some things that we LIKE TO THINK WE KNOW. The first pramana is "Pratyaksa" (Evidence/Perception), if we can see something, we know it is. Then we have "Anumāna" (Inference), if we can logically conclude something, we know it is. Then we have "Upamāna" (Comparison/Analogy), if we can compare something accurately to something that is, we know it is. Then we have "Arthāpatti" (Postulation/Derivation from cirumstance), if things around something point towards the existence of something, we know it is. Then we have "Anupalabdhi" (non-perception/negative cognitive proof), the absence of something that should be and then the absence confirms the existence of "what was" because of it not being there, then... we know it is. Then finally, we have the most important one for our Crusade, "Śabda" (Testimony of past or present reliable experts), that means if a text (a sacred text, maybe) is confirming that something is, we know it is. The reality of E.Y.E is forever changing, forever warping around and confusing truth - the only thing we know for certain is the word of our sacred texts and the words of our mentors; when the sacred texts are lost or the mentor is corrupt, that is where entire fragments of our perceived reality falls apart. When we no longer KNOW SOMETHING - that is when Streum bleeds in and manifests. Streum is Chaos, it confuses and corrupts, not because of a natural Evil, but because we've not exacted Order (or Danda, if we want to continue the Hinduism comparison). A Traitor is a Mentor turned Corrupt, a Reliable Witness turned a Liar, if we can't trust the road ahead, who knows where the Door will open next? The Past makes the Future... and we're in the Past right now, so you better make sure it's in Order before the Future arrives.

So, first things first: If you loved E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy, you will fall in love with this very quickly. All of that incredible warhammer-inspired yet unique aesthetic is here better than ever before, the autistic armored men waiting you on our hub to drop insane lines are all there and I love it. This game plays like a roguelite Vermintide basically. You can upgrade yourself during the run, get new weapons, or get daemonic orbs(the currency to upgrade the Daimon Weapons) to upgrade them permanently. I can't say this combat is better than Vermintide or Darktide, but it's pretty good and functional. Weapons feel heavy and hit hard. You have a stamina bar that you can use to dash or do special ranged attacks, dashes have invulnerability frames, you know the drill. I played like 5 hours but you can tell the game was designed to be played co-op. You have votes to choose the next map, votes for team buffs and things like that, but I played solo for 5 hours and it was pretty decent. Could defeat 3 bosses already on the lowest difficulty(which was not easy guys come on). But as you keep playing, leveling up stats and weapons, you are able to take on stronger enemies. A special thumbs up from me are the bosses. At the start some might feel unfair, especially having to find the secret of some NECROMANCER, but these fights are awesome. They look great, and have cool mechanics that allow player skill to shine. About performance honestly, no complains. I play a mix of high settings lowering shadows and lights and can get consistent 120+ FPS. When ♥♥♥♥ gets real busy frame rates can drop. What I would like to see changed: I would like to see my entire weapon while holding it, specially since you can craft awesome skins. And that annoying bug where you get stuck in nothing get fixed, at happens kind of frequently even for me who played 5 hours. Also please fix the bug where it doesn't save the video configuration. Edit: I played multiplayer with a friend for 2 hours and faced no connection issues or crashes. Keep up the good work guys.

The short: Easy recommend. I'm having a blast! There are SOME bugs and jank, but the game is a lot of fun - and a visual, atmospheric feast! If you're a fan of EYE or StreumOn, your enjoyment likely doubles! It's impressive how far the studio has come. I think the game would have been well worth it even before the price drop, even with all the baggage that comes with early access. ============================= My experience: Initially, I was hesitant. For all it's flaws, I was a fan of the original EYE Divine Cybermancy and wasn't really looking for a Vermintide-like Spin-off. But boy has my tune changed. It still oozes that EYE feeling and that StreumOn weirdness that originally got me hooked. Characters speak Latin. Plenty of EYE references - and still the occasional unapologetically 'StreumOn' dialogue. On that note, SteumOn has MASSIVELY improved. I've seen Early Access games with far more bugs. But more importantly, this game already has few bugs for a StreumOn title. Yes you will find abilities that don't quite trigger right, the level select in multiplayer doesn't always show the right level and sometimes the countdown timer between levels visually disappears. But only once have I run into a run-ending bug. Some people have experienced crashes with Unreal, though, so be warned! The gameplay feels like a mix of Vermintide, and Necromunda: Hired Gun (a previous title from the same studio), but BUTTERY smooth in comparison to that last title! Regular fights are fast, adrenaline pumping horde-fests with the occasional enemies you have to single out. Enemies are visually distinct and varied in what they do - you'll already find enough variety not to get bored. Bosses are approaching a first-person take between FURI and Ikaruga - you'll find yourself double jumping, dashing and blocking to weave between bullets and reflect attacks. The atmosphere, the designs, the music. I fell in love with it all over again. As a prequel to EYE, the studio not only poured ALL that they have learned into the presentation, but gave a lot of background a fresh new paint. The soundtrack is very reminiscent of EYE (though not quite the same) and I am enjoying it greatly. Visually, you've got yourself a mix of the original Divine Cybermancy and Soulframe (which is already pretty out there in design choices). You'll see some pretty wild levels and character designs here, right from the start. Even the story, as piecemeal and souls-like as it is for now, has me invested. I could gush more but... Yeah. I've been hooked. I want more - more of this game, more of StreumOn, and especially, hopefully, perhaps, more Brouzoufs.
PRETTY FUN

As expected from StreumOn, this game is jank as hell (affectionately), but the concept and execution turn a seemingly benign concept into a brilliant horde slasher. It needs a lot of work, and that work is being done, but this game very much carries the DNA of this studio's (arguable) magnum opus E.Y.E. and that is gonna make it somewhat polarizing from the get-go. If you don't mind a game that is both fair, yet brutally unforgiving; riddled with bugs and incomprehensible and/or mistranslated mechanics, but also unexpectedly deep in how those mechanics are applied; then Daimon Blades is the game you never asked for, but always wanted. Dive into the Labyrinth, unleash the power of your Daimon, kill the Hermit, descend the cycles of guilt. Wait, that last one's not right...
Dank/10

Very little changes about your playthrough over the course of the run and between runs. It gets dull quickly. Basic combat is pretty bland, despite the dodge and parry mechanics. I didn't feel the need to change how I engaged with different enemies beyond parry reflecting projectile enemies and chaining heavy attacks on everything else. I'm not sure how much locational damage is going on, as shield-wielding enemies would frequently block my attacks from behind while stunned. Enemy hitboxes are terrible, you can be hit by enemies whiffing the air in front of them while you're behind them, and enemies will phase through your weapon, spawn on top of you, or get stuck in level geometry fairly regularly. Sometimes enemy attacks will blend poorly from hurt reactions/movement, or fail to properly animate at all. I had to use the steam background recording feature a few times to figure out why I lost hitpoints (which is how I realized how bad some of the hitboxes apparently are). English localization of stats/attributes/abilities/effects is terrible, frequently unclear or straight wrong. Some attributes appear to do nothing. The weird "strategy phase" midway through runs feels out of place. Upon completing the run, I felt no desire to play again. Despite all the janky combat it's still fairly trivial to be invincible and the game does not feel very challenging. On the positive side the game's overall aesthetic and environments are interesting and high quality. The fairly samey proc-gen layouts make it lose its luster fairly quickly, though. That is about all I enjoyed.
